svg.title: Nut preload methods
svg.text: Nut preload methods – remove backlash and raise rigidity (preload Fpr = 3 % Ca = 1 140 N for BN-3210-FL)
Ball 2 – 6 µm bigger than the groove space →
P1 – P2 (2 – 5 % Ca). Compact, short nut;
more spin friction, max preload limited.
Spacer pushes the nuts apart (tension, O-type):
balls of A touch the left, of B the right flanks.
P2 – P3 (5 – 10 % Ca). Highest rigidity, set by
grinding the spacer; longer + heavier nut.
The nut thread has a lead jump δ (e.g. 0.02 mm)
in the middle: left balls touch one flank, right
balls the other. P1 – P2; short like A, 2-point
contact like B; must be ground into the nut.
Preload – deflection diagram (Hertz: δ ∝ F^(2/3), so F = k·δ^1.5; example δ0 = 4 µm)
Above it the preload is lost.
but more heat and less life. Measure the
preload as drag torque on the test stand.
